name: Lane Use Control (straight or right)
spec: white vertical rectangle with black arrows showing straight-ahead and right-turn movements allowed from the lane
meaning: This lane may go straight or turn as the arrows show.

snippets.back: Flashing or sequencing arrow panels may operate by day or night to direct lane use and indicate a closure ahead.
Lane use control signals hang over individual lanes of a street, highway or freeway to show which lanes you may or may not use.
Do not park facing along a lane used by traffic traveling in the opposite direction.
Double broken yellow lines signal a reversible lane, which differs from a center turn lane used only for left turns.
A bicycle lane uses a white boundary or green pavement together with a bicycle symbol to show preferential bicycle use.
Regulatory signs communicate laws about such matters as direction, lane use, turns, speed and parking.
Lane control signals are mounted over the lane they govern and set the direction of travel in a lane that carries one direction at some times and the opposite direction at others.

Regulatory signs state the rules for direction, lane use, turning, speed, and parking, and a red circle with a slash over a symbol always prohibits something such as a left turn, right turn, or U-turn.

result.summary: No snippet describes a white rectangle with straight/right arrows or states that this lane may go straight or right; closest texts only generally mention lane use control signals/regulatory signs.
